answer_1.quote: In this work, we target global causal connections between events as a means to understanding and reasoning about events, targeting applications such as event likelihood prediction and event forecasting. ... our approach of reasoning over causal graphs yields significantly better predictions and explanations ... We further demonstrate the downstream utility of these causal models for a forecasting task (ForecastQA) and a variant of a narrative cloze task. ... generating narratives in form of text descriptions.
answer_1.outputs: causal graphs and causal explanation chains

answer_2.quote: We measured the performance of different approaches and reported balanced accuracy (BAcc) and Macro F1 (more details in Appendix A.2) results for two settings. ... F1:C, F1:NC are the accuracies of identifying causal and non-causal links respectively.

answer_3.quote: We use the main evaluation question, Can event "EVENT1" cause event "EVENT2"? to directly evaluate each causal relation between event pairs. ... We use GPT-4 for primitive questions since the turn-around time is faster and it requires less communication.

answer_4.quote: However, to verify the GPT-4 results we also did a human evaluation on a subset of the data and observed similar trends. Human evaluation is also not done by ourselves (authors of the paper), but with two external annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked the same primitive evaluation question: Can event "EVENT1" cause event "EVENT2"?
